title: Codebook wording review: Shared lists, rules and conventions
background:
Review round 4 of the codebook wording. You chose on 30 October that agents draft the missing value definitions and you review every wording slot here. This page covers **shared lists, rules and conventions**.

Each card is one codebook item. Open "Show the wording slots" to read them. Each slot is labelled with where its text came from:

- **Plan text**
- **New agent draft (round 4)**
- **Option text you chose in round 3**
- **Agent edit of the signed questionnaire**
- **Text you approved on 30 October**
- **Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete**

Answer per item: approve all, approve with line-edits or deletions in the comments (by slot number), or ask for a redraft. Deletion is open only for old version-2.5 slots and for one slot of each overlap pair. The batch card at the top approves everything you leave unmarked. No recommendation is given on any wording.

New agent drafts carry a certainty mark; those marked **Needs your decision** rest on no ruling or text for some point.

**One slot needs your sentence:** the support status "Not required" (card F1).

items.title: Shared list: missing-answer labels
items.situation: 7 slots: 1 × plan text; 4 × option text you chose in round 3; 1 × text you approved on 30 October; 1 × agent edit of the signed questionnaire.
items.body:
**1. Wording** — Plan text, from the specification
Missing-value tokens: one reserved set of four: "not asked" (`not_applicable` renamed "not asked" everywhere, T2) when a rule skipped the question; "not documented"; "unknown"; and `_NA_` for items on a row that has no activity (all-01 b). [wording: PI — RC-D-003 §1: the `_NA_` definition] The temporary part answer of R-044 is not a reserved token. Exception: on pages whose verdict shows no GenAI, the description items and `content_data` take `no`, not "not asked" (page-09 c; R-003). New and non-frozen fields adopt it; frozen CX items keep their signed spellings with a mapping row; spellings are fixed before the version steps. [wording: PI — RC-D-002 N4: token spellings]

**2. Label for rows with no activity** — Option text you chose in round 3
Store `not_asked` when a rule skips a question; store `_NA_` on items of a row that has no activity.

**3. Published-summary map** — Option text you chose in round 3
Keep them as values when coding; map them onto "unknown" in published summaries.

**4. Published-summary map (label text)** — Option text you chose in round 3
Treat "unresolved" and "not assessable" as missing answers, reported as "unknown"

**5. Published-summary map (institution rule)** — Text you approved on 30 October
Inside the institution-level rule both keep their current roles, and `not_assessable` stays out of the institution-rate base (O15).

**6. Questionnaire map row** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
Missing-answer labels. The signed spellings of these items are kept, and each maps to one of the codebook's reserved labels: "not asked" (ruled out by a rule), "not documented" (page silent), "unknown" (stated but undeterminable, or downgraded). Map: `unknown` of `disclosure_form` (CX-17) and of `disclosure_scope` (CX-24) → "unknown"; `unclear` of `evaluation_documented` (CX-33) → "unknown"; `not_documented` (CX-34) → "not documented"; `no` of the `evaluation_type_*` and `content_*` items → "not documented"; `none_reported` (CX-60, CX-61) → "not documented". Where these rows say an item is not asked (CX-25, CX-41, CX-51), it stores the reserved "not asked" label.

**7. Where the map row lives** — Option text you chose in round 3
Keep the new map row in the questionnaire; keep the "narrowed in" marks.

items.title: Shared list: how we know
items.situation: 7 slots: 3 × option text you chose in round 3; 3 × new agent draft (round 4); 1 × plan text.
items.body:
**1. Value `stated`** — Option text you chose in round 3
"Stated" = the page says it, whoever copied it

**2. Value `from_metadata`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The value comes from the page's metadata or its web address, or is the date the page was fetched; it is not read from the page text.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**3. Value `looked_up`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The value was found in a source other than the page itself, such as a web archive's record of when the page first appeared.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: The only ruled example is the archive date; 'a source other than the page' generalises it._

**4. Value `derived`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The value is computed by a rule from other coded values; it is not stated on the page or looked up.
_Draft certainty: medium._

**5. Value `quoted_by_quote_step`** — Option text you chose in round 3
"quoted by the quote step" = only the quote step's copy.

**6. Wording** — Plan text, from review round 2
Every 'how we know' field uses the same five values: stated, from metadata, looked up, derived, quoted by the quote step. The per-run version record also holds the codebook version, the channel tag stays on each row, and per-code coder details are stored internally and linked to that record.

**7. Date-origin map** — Option text you chose in round 3
Web address to from metadata; page quote to quoted by the quote step; archive bound to looked up; unknown through the missing-answer labels; access date to from metadata; add a yes/no note "this date is an upper bound".

items.title: Shared rule: activity unit
items.situation: 1 slots: 1 × plan text.
items.body:
**1. 0** — Plan text, from the specification
One activity = one action (deployment, governance instrument, staff training) by one actor concerning one tool or instrument. A named program is one activity; each named component is its own activity, linked to the program as a component of it. Repeated transactions for the same product by the same unit are one activity. A policy and the tools it approves are separate activities, linked by a "governs" relation.

items.title: Shared rule: cx grain
items.situation: 5 slots: 5 × agent edit of the signed questionnaire.
items.body:
**1. 0** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
**Page fields** (`disclosure_form`, `disclosure_scope`, the optional `content_*` items) are properties of the source page. They are coded once per (institution × page), on the stored page text the item declares as its input (the main text unless the item states otherwise), and copied to every evidence row from that page. The `content_*` items that CX-51 and CX-52 mark as derived are not asked; they are computed once per page from the codes of the activities on that page.

**2. 1** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
**Finding fields** (`evaluation_documented`, optional `evaluation_type_*`, and the outcome and incident items of CX-61) are coded per (finding × page). The state given to jev is the page text plus that finding's `activity_name`, `activity_type`, `adoption_stage` and `tool_name`. The state of each question set (its fields, their order and the chunk marker) is pinned in the codebook and is part of the frozen instrument; any change to it counts as a wording change.

**3. 2** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
Code what the page says. Never use outside knowledge of the institution, the country's laws or the register system.

**4. 3** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
The codebook stores page-level and finding × page codes only. How page codes roll up to a finding, institution or country is an index decision (index decisions 6–8), not a codebook rule.

**5. 4** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
The raw jev answer is stored with its probability distribution, confidence, response model id and request id.

items.title: Long-page convention: check then combine
items.situation: 3 slots: 1 × agent edit of the signed questionnaire; 2 × option text you chose in round 3.
items.body:
**1. Wording** — Agent edit of the signed questionnaire
Each part's answer is checked (quote, 0.8 bar) before combining; downgraded parts enter as their downgrade target (`unknown`), except page verdicts, which keep their value and the downgraded tag (r2#40).

**2. Wording** — Option text you chose in round 3
Each part is checked as drafted; the prompt states the text is only part of the document; every question gets a temporary value "not covered by this part"; such parts do not vote when parts are combined; if every part gives it, the page is "not documented"; the temporary value is never published.

**3. Wording** — Option text you chose in round 3
